- **Individual Cryptography**
  2023-01-24 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/088)
  Stefan Dziembowski, Sebastian Faust, Tomasz Lizurej

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  We initiate a formal study of individual cryptography. Informally speaking, an algorithm $\mathsf{Alg}$ is &quot;individual&quot; if, in every implementation of $\mathsf{Alg}$, there always exists an individual user with full knowledge of the cryptographic data $S$ used by $\mathsf{Alg}$. In particular, it should be infeasible to design implementations of this algorithm that would hide $S$ by distributing it between a group of parties using an MPC protocol or outsourcing it to a trusted execution environment. We define and construct two primitives in this model. The first one, called &quot;proofs of individual knowledge&quot;, is a tool for proving that a given message is fully known to a single (&quot;individual&quot;) machine on the Internet, i.e., it cannot be shared between a group of parties. The second one, dubbed &quot;individual secret sharing&quot;, is a scheme for sharing a secret $S$ between a group of parties so that the parties have no knowledge of $S$ as long as they do not reconstruct it. The reconstruction ensures that if the shareholders attempt to collude, one of them will learn the secret entirely. Individual secret sharing has applications for preventing collusion in secret sharing. A central technique for constructing individual cryptographic primitives is the concept of MPC hardness. MPC hardness precludes an adversary from completing a cryptographic task in a distributed fashion within a specific time frame.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing; TEE: trusted execution environment

  </details>

- **Complete Knowledge: Preventing Encumbrance of Cryptographic Secrets**
  2023-01-15 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2023/044)
  Mahimna Kelkar, Kushal Babel, Philip Daian, James Austgen, Vitalik Buterin, Ari Juels

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Most cryptographic protocols model a player’s knowledge of secrets in a simple way. Informally, the player knows a secret in the sense that she can directly furnish it as a (private) input to a protocol, e.g., to digitally sign a message. The growing availability of Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) and secure multiparty computation, however, undermines this model of knowledge. Such tools can encumber a secret sk and permit a chosen player to access sk conditionally, without actually knowing sk. By permitting selective access to sk by an adversary, encumbrance of secrets can enable vote-selling in cryptographic voting schemes, illegal sale of credentials for online services, and erosion of deniability in anonymous messaging systems. Unfortunately, existing proof-of-knowledge protocols fail to demonstrate that a secret is unencumbered. We therefore introduce and formalize a new notion called complete knowledge (CK). A proof (or argument) of CK shows that a prover does not just know a secret, but also has fully unencumbered knowledge, i.e., unrestricted ability to use the secret. We introduce two practical CK schemes that use special-purpose hardware, specifically TEEs and off-the-shelf mining ASICs. We prove the security of these schemes and explore their practical deployment with a complete, end-to-end prototype with smart-contract verification that supports both. We show how CK can address encumbrance attacks identified in previous work. Finally, we introduce two new applications enabled by CK that involve proving ownership of blockchain assets.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure multiparty computation; TEE: trusted execution environments

  </details>

- **HAAC: A Hardware-Software Co-Design to Accelerate Garbled Circuits**
  2023 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.13324) · [ISCA](https://doi.org/10.1145/3579371.3589045)
  Brandon Reagen, Jianqiao Mo, Jayanth Gopinath

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Privacy and security have rapidly emerged as priorities in system design. One powerful solution for providing both is privacy-preserving computation, where functions are computed directly on encrypted data and control can be provided over how data is used. Garbled circuits (GCs) are a PPC technology that provide both confidential computing and control over how data is used. The challenge is that they incur significant performance overheads compared to plaintext. This paper proposes a novel garbled circuits accelerator and compiler, named HAAC, to mitigate performance overheads and make privacy-preserving computation more practical. HAAC is a hardware-software co-design. GCs are exemplars of co-design as programs are completely known at compile time, i.e., all dependence, memory accesses, and control flow are fixed. The design philosophy of HAAC is to keep hardware simple and efficient, maximizing area devoted to our proposed custom execution units and other circuits essential for high performance (e.g., on-chip storage). The compiler can leverage its program understanding to realize hardware&#x27;s performance potential by generating effective instruction schedules, data layouts, and orchestrating off-chip events. In taking this approach we can achieve ASIC performance/efficiency without sacrificing generality. Insights of our approach include how co-design enables expressing arbitrary GCs programs as streams, which simplifies hardware and enables complete memory-compute decoupling, and the development of a scratchpad that captures data reuse by tracking program execution, eliminating the need for costly hardware managed caches and tagging logic. We evaluate HAAC with VIP-Bench and achieve an average speedup of 589$\times$ with DDR4 (2,627$\times$ with HBM2) in 4.3mm$^2$ of area.

  匹配依据：MPC: garbled circuits; TEE: confidential computing

  </details>

### 2022

- **ORTOA: One Round Trip Oblivious Access**
  2022-11-01 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1506)
  Sujaya Maiyya, Yuval Steinhart, Divyakant Agrawal, Prabhanjan Ananth, Amr El Abbadi

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Many applications relying on cloud storage services typically encrypt their data to ensure data privacy. However, reading or writing the encrypted data to serve client requests reveals the type of client operation to a potentially untrusted cloud. An adversary can exploit this information leak to compromise a user’s privacy by tracking read/write access patterns. Existing approaches such as Oblivious RAM (ORAM) schemes hide the type of client access by always reading and then writing the data sequentially for both reads and writes, rendering one of these rounds redundant with respect to a client request. To mitigate this redundancy, we propose ORTOA- a family of protocols enabling single-round data access on remote storage without revealing the operation type. Specifically, we propose three protocols, two using existing cryptographic primitives of fully homomorphic encryption and trusted execution environments (TEEs), and a new primitive inspired by garbled circuits. Each of these protocols has different trust assumptions, allowing an application to choose the option best suited for its needs. To our knowledge, ORTOA is the first to propose generalized protocols to obfuscate the type of access in a single round, reducing the communication overhead in half. The proposed techniques can pave the way for novel ORAM schemes that hide both the type of access and the access pattern in a single round. Our experimental results show ORTOA achieving throughput gains of 1.7x-3.2x compared to a baseline requiring two rounds for access type concealment, with the baseline incurring latency 1.5-1.9x that of ORTOA for 160B-sized objects.

  匹配依据：MPC: garbled circuits; TEE: trusted execution environments

  </details>

- **Bool Network: An Open, Distributed, Secure Cross-chain Notary Platform**
  2022-09-28 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/1290)
  Zeyuan Yin, Bingsheng Zhang, Jingzhong Xu, Kaiyu Lu, Kui Ren

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  With the advancement of blockchain technology, hundreds of cryptocurrencies have been deployed. The bloom of heterogeneous blockchain platforms brings a new emerging problem: typically, various blockchains are isolated systems, how to securely identify and/or transfer digital properties across blockchains? There are three main kinds of cross-chain approaches: sidechains/relays, notaries, and hashed time-lock contracts. Among them, notary-based cross-chain solutions have the best compatibility and user-friendliness, but they are typically centralized. To resolve this issue, we present Bool Network -- an open, distributed, secure cross-chain notary platform powered by MPC-based distributed key management over evolving hidden committees. More specifically, to protect the identities of the committee members, we propose a Ring verifiable random function (Ring VRF) protocol, where the real public key of a VRF instance can be hidden among a ring, which may be of independent interest to other cryptographic protocols. Furthermore, all the key management procedures are executed in the TEE, such as Intel SGX, to ensure the privacy and integrity of partial key components. A prototype of the proposed Bool Network is implemented in Rust language, using Polkadot Substrate.

  匹配依据：MPC: mpc (context); TEE: intel sgx

  </details>

- **CoVault: A Secure Analytics Platform**
  2022-08-07 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.03784)
  Roberta De Viti, Isaac Sheff, Noemi Glaeser, Baltasar Dinis, Rodrigo Rodrigues, Bobby Bhattacharjee, Anwar Hithnawi, Deepak Garg, Peter Druschel

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Analytics on personal data, such as individuals&#x27; mobility, financial, and health data can be of significant benefit to society. Such data is already collected by smartphones, apps and services today, but liberal societies have so far refrained from making it available for large-scale analytics. Arguably, this is due at least in part to the lack of an analytics platform that can secure data through transparent, technical means (ideally with decentralized trust), enforce source policies, handle millions of distinct data sources, and run queries on billions of records with acceptable query latencies. To bridge this gap, we present an analytics platform called CoVault which combines secure multi-party computation (MPC) with trusted execution environment (TEE)-based delegation of trust to be able execute approved queries on encrypted data contributed by individuals within a datacenter to achieve the above properties. We show that CoVault scales well despite the high cost of MPC. For example, CoVault can process data relevant to epidemic analytics for a country of 80M people (about 11.85B data records/day) on a continuous basis using a core pair for every 20,000 people. Compared to a state-of-the-art MPC-based platform, CoVault can process queries between 7 to over 100 times faster, as well as scale to many sources and big data.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure multi party computation; TEE: trusted execution environment

  </details>

- **Paras - A Private NFT Protocol**
  2022-07-30 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/976)
  Vanishree Rao

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Non-fungible tokens (NFTs) are a blockchain application that has recently witnessed significant success. However, NFT marketplaces are majorly built on popular blockchain platforms that do not provide privacy tools. As a result, NFTs are easily visible to everyone. This has naturally given rise to various issues, including stolen/duplicate NFTs and attacks like shill trading. Furthermore, this architecture fails to reflect the real-life privacy notion as it digitizes unique physical goods. In this project, we build Paras - a blockchain-agnostic protocol that offers privacy to NFTs. Specifically, one may hide the real NFTs and only display a reference to them on marketplaces, hide seller and bidder identities, hide bid values and user wallet balances. Paras is based on cryptographic primitives, such as, threshold encryption and robust secret sharing. It does not rely on any trusted execution environments for security, unlike some existing protocols in this direction.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing; TEE: trusted execution environments

  </details>

- **Towards Practical Privacy-Preserving Solution for Outsourced Neural Network Inference**
  2022-06-06 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.02384)
  Pinglan Liu, Wensheng Zhang

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  When neural network model and data are outsourced to cloud server for inference, it is desired to preserve the confidentiality of model and data as the involved parties (i.e., cloud server, model providing client and data providing client) may not trust mutually. Solutions were proposed based on multi-party computation, trusted execution environment (TEE) and leveled or fully homomorphic encryption (LHE/FHE), but their limitations hamper practical application. We propose a new framework based on synergistic integration of LHE and TEE, which enables collaboration among mutually-untrusted three parties, while minimizing the involvement of (relatively) resource-constrained TEE and allowing the full utilization of the untrusted but more resource-rich part of server. We also propose a generic and efficient LHE-based inference scheme as an important performance-determining component of the framework. We implemented/evaluated the proposed system on a moderate platform and show that, our proposed scheme is more applicable/scalable to various settings, and has better performance, compared to the state-of-the-art LHE-based solutions.

  匹配依据：MPC: multi party computation; TEE: trusted execution environment

  </details>

- **Training Differentially Private Models with Secure Multiparty Computation**
  2022-02-12 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.02625) · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2022/146)
  Sikha Pentyala, Davis Railsback, Ricardo Maia, Rafael Dowsley, David Melanson, Anderson Nascimento, Martine De Cock

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  We address the problem of learning a machine learning model from training data that originates at multiple data owners while providing formal privacy guarantees regarding the protection of each owner&#x27;s data. Existing solutions based on Differential Privacy (DP) achieve this at the cost of a drop in accuracy. Solutions based on Secure Multiparty Computation (MPC) do not incur such accuracy loss but leak information when the trained model is made publicly available. We propose an MPC solution for training DP models. Our solution relies on an MPC protocol for model training, and an MPC protocol for perturbing the trained model coefficients with Laplace noise in a privacy-preserving manner. The resulting MPC+DP approach achieves higher accuracy than a pure DP approach while providing the same formal privacy guarantees. Our work obtained first place in the iDASH2021 Track III competition on confidential computing for secure genome analysis.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure multiparty computation; TEE: confidential computing

  </details>

- **Hybrid Trust Multi-party Computation with Trusted Execution Environment.**
  2022 · MPC / TEE · [NDSS](https://www.ndss-symposium.org/ndss-paper/auto-draft-222/)
  Jianting Ning, Jiamin Shen, Hongbing Wang, Ee-Chien Chang, Pengfei Wu

### 2021

- **CHEX-MIX: Combining Homomorphic Encryption with Trusted Execution Environments for Two-party Oblivious Inference in the Cloud**
  2021-12-09 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/1603)
  Deepika Natarajan, Andrew Loveless, Wei Dai, Ronald Dreslinski

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Data, when coupled with state-of-the-art machine learning models, can enable remarkable applications. But, there exists an underlying tension: users wish to keep their data private, and model providers wish to protect their intellectual property. Homomorphic encryption (HE) and multi-party computation (MPC) techniques have been proposed as solutions to this problem; however, both techniques require model providers to fully trust the server performing the machine learning computation. This limits the scale of inference applications, since it prevents model providers from leveraging shared public cloud infrastructures. In this work, we present CHEX-MIX, a solution to the problem of privacy-preserving machine learning between two mutually distrustful parties in an untrusted cloud setting. CHEX-MIX relies on a combination of HE and trusted execution environments (TEEs), using HE to provide clients with confidentiality guarantees, and TEEs to provide model providers with confidentiality guarantees and protect the integrity of computation from malicious cloud adversaries. Unlike prior solutions to this problem, such as multi-key HE, single-key HE, MPC, or TEE-only techniques, our solution assumes that both the client and the cloud can be malicious, makes no collusion assumptions, and frees model providers from needing to maintain private online infrastructures. Our results show that CHEX-MIX can execute at high efficiency, with low communication cost, while providing security guarantees unaddressed by prior work. Compared to a recent multi-key HE work that allows partial cloud offload, for example, CHEX-MIX achieves a 3× lower communication cost and a 3× faster computation time.

  匹配依据：MPC: multi party computation; TEE: trusted execution environments

  </details>

- **Flatee: Federated Learning Across Trusted Execution Environments**
  2021-11-12 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.06867)
  Arup Mondal, Yash More, Ruthu Hulikal Rooparaghunath, Debayan Gupta

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Federated learning allows us to distributively train a machine learning model where multiple parties share local model parameters without sharing private data. However, parameter exchange may still leak information. Several approaches have been proposed to overcome this, based on multi-party computation, fully homomorphic encryption, etc.; many of these protocols are slow and impractical for real-world use as they involve a large number of cryptographic operations. In this paper, we propose the use of Trusted Execution Environments (TEE), which provide a platform for isolated execution of code and handling of data, for this purpose. We describe Flatee, an efficient privacy-preserving federated learning framework across TEEs, which considerably reduces training and communication time. Our framework can handle malicious parties (we do not natively solve adversarial data poisoning, though we describe a preliminary approach to handle this).

  匹配依据：MPC: multi party computation; TEE: trusted execution environments

  </details>

- **PIM-Enclave: Bringing Confidential Computation Inside Memory**
  2021-11-05 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.03307)
  Kha Dinh Duy, Hojoon Lee

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Demand for data-intensive workloads and confidential computing are the prominent research directions shaping the future of cloud computing. Computer architectures are evolving to accommodate the computing of large data better. Protecting the computation of sensitive data is also an imperative yet challenging objective; processor-supported secure enclaves serve as the key element in confidential computing in the cloud. However, side-channel attacks are threatening their security boundaries. The current processor architectures consume a considerable portion of its cycles in moving data. Near data computation is a promising approach that minimizes redundant data movement by placing computation inside storage. In this paper, we present a novel design for Processing-In-Memory (PIM) as a data-intensive workload accelerator for confidential computing. Based on our observation that moving computation closer to memory can achieve efficiency of computation and confidentiality of the processed information simultaneously, we study the advantages of confidential computing \emph{inside} memory. We then explain our security model and programming model developed for PIM-based computation offloading. We construct our findings into a software-hardware co-design, which we call PIM-Enclave. Our design illustrates the advantages of PIM-based confidential computing acceleration. Our evaluation shows PIM-Enclave can provide a side-channel resistant secure computation offloading and run data-intensive applications with negligible performance overhead compared to baseline PIM model.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure computation; TEE: confidential computing, secure enclaves

  </details>

- **GPS: Integration of Graphene, PALISADE, and SGX for Large-scale Aggregations of Distributed Data**
  2021-09-14 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/1155)
  Jonathan Takeshita, Colin McKechney, Justin Pajak, Antonis Papadimitriou, Ryan Karl, Taeho Jung

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Secure computing methods such as fully homomorphic encryption and hardware solutions such as Intel Software Guard Extension (SGX) have been applied to provide security for user input in privacy-oriented computation outsourcing. Fully homomorphic encryption is amenable to parallelization and hardware acceleration to improve its scalability and latency, but is limited in the complexity of functions it can efficiently evaluate. SGX is capable of arbitrarily complex calculations, but due to expensive memory paging and context switches, computations in SGX are bound by practical limits. These limitations make either of fully homomorphic encryption or SGX alone unsuitable for large-scale multi-user computations with complex intermediate calculations. In this paper, we present GPS, a novel framework integrating the Graphene, PALISADE, and SGX technologies. GPS combines the scalability of homomorphic encryption with the arbitrary computational abilities of SGX, forming a more functional and efficient system for outsourced secure computations with large numbers of users. We implement GPS using linear regression training as an instantiation, and our experimental results indicate a base speedup of 1.03x to 8.69x (depending on computation parameters) over an SGX-only linear regression training without multithreading or hardware acceleration. Experiments and projections show improvements over the SGX-only training of 3.28x to 10.43x using multithreading and 4.99x to 12.67 with GPU acceleration.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure computing; TEE: sgx

  </details>

- **undeSErVed trust: Exploiting Permutation-Agnostic Remote Attestation**
  2021-06-29 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.15387)
  Luca Wilke, Jan Wichelmann, Florian Sieck, Thomas Eisenbarth

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  The ongoing trend of moving data and computation to the cloud is met with concerns regarding privacy and protection of intellectual property. Cloud Service Providers (CSP) must be fully trusted to not tamper with or disclose processed data, hampering adoption of cloud services for many sensitive or critical applications. As a result, CSPs and CPU manufacturers are rushing to find solutions for secure outsourced computation in the Cloud. While enclaves, like Intel SGX, are strongly limited in terms of throughput and size, AMD&#x27;s Secure Encrypted Virtualization (SEV) offers hardware support for transparently protecting code and data of entire VMs, thus removing the performance, memory and software adaption barriers of enclaves. Through attestation of boot code integrity and means for securely transferring secrets into an encrypted VM, CSPs are effectively removed from the list of trusted entities. There have been several attacks on the security of SEV, by abusing I/O channels to encrypt and decrypt data, or by moving encrypted code blocks at runtime. Yet, none of these attacks have targeted the attestation protocol, the core of the secure computing environment created by SEV. We show that the current attestation mechanism of Zen 1 and Zen 2 architectures has a significant flaw, allowing us to manipulate the loaded code without affecting the attestation outcome. An attacker may abuse this weakness to inject arbitrary code at startup -- and thus take control over the entire VM execution, without any indication to the VM&#x27;s owner. Our attack primitives allow the attacker to do extensive modifications to the bootloader and the operating system, like injecting spy code or extracting secret data. We present a full end-to-end attack, from the initial exploit to leaking the key of the encrypted disk image during boot, giving the attacker unthrottled access to all of the VM&#x27;s persistent data.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure computing; TEE: intel sgx, secure encrypted virtualization

  </details>

- **Cloak: Transitioning States on Legacy Blockchains Using Secure and Publicly Verifiable Off-Chain Multi-Party Computation**
  2021-06-26 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.13926)
  Qian Ren, Yingjun Wu, Han Liu, Yue Li, Anne Victor, Hong Lei, Lei Wang, Bangdao Chen

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  In recent years, the confidentiality of smart contracts has become a fundamental requirement for practical applications. While many efforts have been made to develop architectural capabilities for enforcing confidential smart contracts, a few works arise to extend confidential smart contracts to Multi-Party Computation (MPC), i.e., multiple parties jointly evaluate a transaction off-chain and commit the outputs on-chain without revealing their secret inputs/outputs to each other. However, existing solutions lack public verifiability and require O(n) transactions to enable negotiation or resist adversaries, thus suffering from inefficiency and compromised security. In this paper, we propose Cloak, a framework for enabling Multi-Party Transaction (MPT) on existing blockchains. An MPT refers to transitioning blockchain states by an publicly verifiable off-chain MPC. We identify and handle the challenges of securing MPT by harmonizing TEE and blockchain. Consequently, Cloak secures the off-chain nondeterministic negotiation process (a party joins an MPT without knowing identities or the total number of parties until the MPT proposal settles), achieves public verifiability (the public can validate that the MPT correctly handles the secret inputs/outputs from multiple parties and reads/writes states on-chain), and resists Byzantine adversaries. According to our proof, Cloak achieves better security with only 2 transactions, superior to previous works that achieve compromised security at O(n) transactions cost. By evaluating examples and real-world MPTs, the gas cost of Cloak reduces by 32.4% on average.

  匹配依据：MPC: multi party computation; TEE: tee (context)

  </details>

- **Private Signaling**
  2021-06-24 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/853)
  Varun Madathil, Alessandra Scafuro, István András Seres, Omer Shlomovits, Denis Varlakov

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  We introduce the problem of private signaling. In this problem, a sender posts a message to a certain location of a public bulletin board, and then computes a signal that allows only the intended recipient (and no one else) to learn that it is the recipient of the posted message. Besides privacy, this problem has the following crucial efficiency requirements. First, the sender and recipient do not participate in any out-of-band communication, and second, the overhead of the recipient should be asymptotically better than scanning the entire board. Existing techniques, such as the server-aided fuzzy message detection (Beck et al., CCS’21), could be employed to solve the private signaling problem. However, this solution requires that the computational effort of the recipient grows with the amount of privacy desired, providing no saving over scanning the entire board if the maximum privacy is required. In this work, we present a server-aided solution to the private signaling problem that guar- antees full privacy for all recipients, while requiring only constant amount of work for both the recipient and the sender. We provide the following contributions. First, we provide a formal definition of private signaling in the Universal Composability (UC) framework and show that it generalizes several real-world settings where recipient anonymity is desired. Second, we present two protocols that UC-realize our definition: one using a single server equipped with a trusted execution environment, and one based on two servers that employs garbled circuits. Third, we provide an open-source implementation of both of our protocols and evaluate their performance and show that they are practical.

  匹配依据：MPC: garbled circuits; TEE: trusted execution environment

  </details>

- **SSS-PRNU: Privacy-Preserving PRNU Based Camera Attribution using Shamir Secret Sharing**
  2021-06-13 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.07029)
  Riyanka Jena, Priyanka Singh, Manoranjan Mohanty

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Photo Response Non-Uniformity(PRNU) noise has proven to be very effective tool in camera based forensics. It helps to match a photo to the device that clicked it. In today&#x27;s scenario, where millions and millions of images are uploaded every hour, it is very easy to compute this unique PRNU pattern from a couple of shared images on social profiles. This endangers the privacy of the camera owner and becomes a cause of major concern for the privacy-aware society. We propose SSS-PRNU scheme that facilitates the forensic investigators to carry out their crime investigation without breaching the privacy of the people. Thus, maintaining a balance between the two. To preserve privacy, extraction of camera fingerprint and PRNU noise for a suspicious image is computed in a trusted execution environment such as ARM TrustZone. After extraction, the sensitive information of camera fingerprint and PRNU noise is distributed into multiple obfuscated shares using Shamir secret sharing(SSS) scheme. These shares are information-theoretically secure and leak no information of underlying content. The encrypted information is distributed to multiple third-part servers where correlation is computed on a share basis between the camera fingerprint and the PRNU noise. These partial correlation values are combined together to obtain the final correlation value that becomes the basis for a match decision. Transforming the computation of the correlation value in the encrypted domain and making it well suited for a distributed environment is the main contribution of the paper. Experiment results validate the feasibility of the proposed scheme that provides a secure framework for PRNU based source camera attribution. The security analysis and evaluation of computational and storage overheads are performed to analysis the practical feasibility of the scheme.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing; TEE: trusted execution environment, trustzone

  </details>

- **SoK: Opportunities for Software-Hardware-Security Codesign for Next Generation Secure Computing**
  2021-05-02 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.00378)
  Deeksha Dangwal, Meghan Cowan, Armin Alaghi, Vincent T. Lee, Brandon Reagen, Caroline Trippel

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Users are demanding increased data security. As a result, security is rapidly becoming a first-order design constraint in next generation computing systems. Researchers and practitioners are exploring various security technologies to meet user demand such as trusted execution environments (e.g., Intel SGX, ARM TrustZone), homomorphic encryption, and differential privacy. Each technique provides some degree of security, but differs with respect to threat coverage, performance overheads, as well as implementation and deployment challenges. In this paper, we present a systemization of knowledge (SoK) on these design considerations and trade-offs using several prominent security technologies. Our study exposes the need for \textit{software-hardware-security} codesign to realize efficient and effective solutions of securing user data. In particular, we explore how design considerations across applications, hardware, and security mechanisms must be combined to overcome fundamental limitations in current technologies so that we can minimize performance overhead while achieving sufficient threat model coverage. Finally, we propose a set of guidelines to facilitate putting these secure computing technologies into practice.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure computing; TEE: intel sgx, trusted execution environments, trustzone

  </details>

- **Cryptonomial: A Framework for Private Time-Series Polynomial Calculations**
  2021-04-15 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/473)
  Ryan Karl, Jonathan Takeshita, Alamin Mohammed, Aaron Striegel, Taeho Jung

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  In modern times, data collected from multi-user distributed applications must be analyzed on a massive scale to support critical business objectives. While analytics often requires the use of personal data, it may compromise user privacy expectations if this analysis is conducted over plaintext data. Private Stream Aggregation (PSA) allows for the aggregation of time-series data, while still providing strong privacy guarantees, and is significantly more efficient over a network than related techniques (e.g. homomorphic encryption, secure multiparty computation, etc.) due to its asynchronous and efficient protocols. However, PSA protocols face limitations and can only compute basic functions, such as sum, average, etc.. We present Cryptonomial, a framework for converting any PSA scheme amenable to a complex canonical embedding into a secure computation protocol that can compute any function over time-series data that can be written as a multivariate polynomial, by combining PSA and a Trusted Execution Environment. This design allows us to compute the parallelizable sections of our protocol outside the TEE using advanced hardware, that can take better advantage of parallelism. We show that Cryptonomial inherits the security requirements of PSA, and supports fully malicious security. We simulate our scheme, and show that our techniques enable performance that is orders of magnitude faster than similar work supporting polynomial calculations.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure computation, secure multiparty computation; TEE: trusted execution environment

  </details>

- **Secure Fast Evaluation of Iterative Methods: With an Application to Secure PageRank**
  2021-03-01 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2021/207)
  Daniele Cozzo, Nigel P. Smart, Younes Talibi Alaoui

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Iterative methods are a standard technique in many areas of scientific computing. The key idea is that a function is applied repeatedly until the resulting sequence converges to the correct answer. When applying such methods in a secure computation methodology (for example using MPC, FHE, or SGX) one either needs to perform enough steps to ensure convergence irrespective of the input data, or one needs to perform a convergence test within the algorithm, and this itself leads to a leakage of data. Using the Banach Fixed Point theorem, and its extensions, we show that this data-leakage can be quantified. We then apply this to a secure (via MPC) implementation of the PageRank methodology. For PageRank we show that allowing this small amount of data-leakage produces a much more efficient secure implementation, and that for many underlying graphs this `leakage&#x27; is already known to any attacker.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure computation; TEE: sgx

  </details>

- **Secure Computing Enclaves Using FPGAs.**
  2021 · MPC / TEE · [TDSC](https://doi.org/10.1109/TDSC.2019.2933214)
  Mohammed Alasli, Marwan H. Abu-Amara, Muhammad E. S. Elrabaa

### 2020

- **PCT-TEE: Trajectory-based Private Contact Tracing System with Trusted Execution Environment**
  2020-12-07 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.03782)
  Fumiyuki Kato, Yang Cao, Masatoshi Yoshikawa

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Existing Bluetooth-based Private Contact Tracing (PCT) systems can privately detect whether people have come into direct contact with COVID-19 patients. However, we find that the existing systems lack functionality and flexibility, which may hurt the success of the contact tracing. Specifically, they cannot detect indirect contact (e.g., people may be exposed to coronavirus because of used the same elevator even without direct contact); they also cannot flexibly change the rules of &quot;risky contact&quot;, such as how many hours of exposure or how close to a COVID-19 patient that is considered as risk exposure, which may be changed with the environmental situation. In this paper, we propose an efficient and secure contact tracing system that enables both direct contact and indirect contact. To address the above problems, we need to utilize users&#x27; trajectory data for private contact tracing, which we call trajectory-based PCT. We formalize this problem as Spatiotemporal Private Set Intersection. By analyzing different approaches such as homomorphic encryption that could be extended to solve this problem, we identify that Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) is a proposing method to achieve our requirements. The major challenge is how to design algorithms for spatiotemporal private set intersection under limited secure memory of TEE. To this end, we design a TEE-based system with flexible trajectory data encoding algorithms. Our experiments on real-world data show that the proposed system can process thousands of queries on tens of million records of trajectory data in a few seconds.

  匹配依据：MPC: private set intersection; TEE: trusted execution environment

  </details>

- **A Systematic Comparison of Encrypted Machine Learning Solutions for Image Classification**
  2020-11-10 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.05296)
  Veneta Haralampieva, Daniel Rueckert, Jonathan Passerat-Palmbach

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  This work provides a comprehensive review of existing frameworks based on secure computing techniques in the context of private image classification. The in-depth analysis of these approaches is followed by careful examination of their performance costs, in particular runtime and communication overhead. To further illustrate the practical considerations when using different privacy-preserving technologies, experiments were conducted using four state-of-the-art libraries implementing secure computing at the heart of the data science stack: PySyft and CrypTen supporting private inference via Secure Multi-Party Computation, TF-Trusted utilising Trusted Execution Environments and HE- Transformer relying on Homomorphic encryption. Our work aims to evaluate the suitability of these frameworks from a usability, runtime requirements and accuracy point of view. In order to better understand the gap between state-of-the-art protocols and what is currently available in practice for a data scientist, we designed three neural network architecture to obtain secure predictions via each of the four aforementioned frameworks. Two networks were evaluated on the MNIST dataset and one on the Malaria Cell image dataset. We observed satisfying performances for TF-Trusted and CrypTen and noted that all frameworks perfectly preserved the accuracy of the corresponding plaintext model.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure computing, secure multi party computation; TEE: trusted execution environments

  </details>

- **Secure and Efficient Trajectory-Based Contact Tracing using Trusted Hardware**
  2020-10-26 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.13381)
  Fumiyuki Kato, Yang Cao, Masatoshi Yoshikawa

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  The COVID-19 pandemic has prompted technological measures to control the spread of the disease. Private contact tracing (PCT) is one of the promising techniques for the purpose. However, the recently proposed Bluetooth-based PCT has several limitations in terms of functionality and flexibility. The existing systems are only able to detect direct contact (i.e., human-human contact), but cannot detect indirect contact (i.e., human-object, such as the disease transmission through surface). Moreover, the rule of risky contact cannot be flexibly changed with the environmental situation and the nature of the virus. In this paper, we propose a secure and efficient trajectory-based PCT system using trusted hardware. We formalize trajectory-based PCT as a generalization of the well-studied Private Set Intersection (PSI), which is mostly based on cryptographic primitives and thus insufficient. We solve the problem by leveraging trusted hardware such as Intel SGX and designing a novel algorithm to achieve a secure, efficient and flexible PCT system. Our experiments on real-world data show that the proposed system can achieve high performance and scalability. Specifically, our system (one single machine with Intel SGX) can process thousands of queries on 100 million records of trajectory data in a few seconds.

  匹配依据：MPC: private set intersection; TEE: intel sgx

  </details>

- **Correlated Randomness Teleportation via Semi-trusted Hardware - Enabling Silent Multi-party Computation**
  2020-10-14 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1259)
  Yibiao Lu, Bingsheng Zhang, Hong-Sheng Zhou, Weiran Liu, Lei Zhang, Kui Ren

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  With the advancement of the trusted execution environment (TEE) technologies, hardware-supported secure computing becomes increasingly popular due to its efficiency. During the protocol execution, typically, the players need to contact a third-party server for remote attestation, ensuring the validity of the involved trusted hardware component, such as Intel SGX, as well as the integrity of the computation result. When the hardware manufacturer is not fully trusted, sensitive information may be leaked to the third-party server through backdoors, steganography, and kleptography, etc. In this work, we introduce a new security notion called semi-trusted hardware model, where the adversary is allowed to passively or maliciously corrupt the hardware. Therefore, she can learn the input of the hardware component and might also tamper its output. We then show how to utilize such semi-trusted hardwares for correlated randomness teleportation. When the semi-trusted hardware is instantiated by Intel SGX, to generate 10k random OT&#x27;s, our protocol is 24X and 450X faster than the EMP-IKNP-ROT in the LAN and WAN setting, respectively. When SGX is used to teleport garbled circuits, the resulting two-party computation protocol is 5.3-5.7X and 43-47X faster than the EMP-SH2PC in the LAN and WAN setting, respectively, for the AES-128, SHA-256, and SHA-512 evaluation. We also show how to achieve malicious security with little overhead.

  匹配依据：MPC: garbled circuits, multi party computation, secure computing, two party computation; TEE: intel sgx, sgx, trusted execution environment

  </details>

- **(F)unctional Sifting: A Privacy-Preserving Reputation System Through Multi-Input Functional Encryption (extended version)**
  2020-10-14 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/1271)
  Alexandros Bakas, Antonis Michalas

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Functional Encryption (FE) allows users who hold a specific secret key (known as the functional key) to learn a specific function of encrypted data whilst learning nothing about the content of the underlying data. Considering this functionality and the fact that the field of FE is still in its infancy, we sought a route to apply this potent tool to solve the existing problem of designing decentralised additive reputation systems. To this end, we first built a symmetric FE scheme for the $\ell_1$ norm of a vector space, which allows us to compute the sum of the components of an encrypted vector (i.e. the votes). Then, we utilized our construction, along with functionalities offered by Intel SGX, to design the first FE-based decentralized additive reputation system with Multi-Party Computation. While our reputation system faces certain limitations, this work is amongst the first attempts that seek to utilize FE in the solution of a real-life problem.

  匹配依据：MPC: multi party computation; TEE: intel sgx

  </details>

- **SAFE: A Secure and Efficient Long-Term Distributed Storage System**
  2020-06-09 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/690)
  Johannes Buchmann, Ghada Dessouky, Tommaso Frassetto, Ágnes Kiss, Ahmad-Reza Sadeghi, Thomas Schneider, Giulia Traverso, Shaza Zeitouni

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Secret sharing-based distributed storage systems are one approach to provide long-term protection of data even against quantum computing. Confidentiality is provided because the shares of data are renewed periodically while integrity is provided by commitment schemes. However, this solution is prohibitively costly and impractical: share renewal requires an information-theoretically secure channel between any two nodes and long-term confidential commitment schemes are computationally impractical for large files. In this paper, we present SAFE, a secret sharing-based long-term secure distributed storage system that leverages a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) to overcome the above limitations. Share generation and renewal are performed inside the TEE and the shares are securely distributed to the storage servers. We prototype SAFE protocols using a TEE instantiation, and show their efficiency, even for large files, compared to existing schemes.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing; TEE: trusted execution environment

  </details>

- **Efficient Oblivious Database Joins**
  2020-03-20 · MPC / TEE · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09481)
  Simeon Krastnikov, Florian Kerschbaum, Douglas Stebila

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  A major algorithmic challenge in designing applications intended for secure remote execution is ensuring that they are oblivious to their inputs, in the sense that their memory access patterns do not leak sensitive information to the server. This problem is particularly relevant to cloud databases that wish to allow queries over the client&#x27;s encrypted data. One of the major obstacles to such a goal is the join operator, which is non-trivial to implement obliviously without resorting to generic but inefficient solutions like Oblivious RAM (ORAM). We present an oblivious algorithm for equi-joins which (up to a logarithmic factor) matches the optimal $O(n\log n)$ complexity of the standard non-secure sort-merge join (on inputs producing $O(n)$ outputs). We do not use use expensive primitives like ORAM or rely on unrealistic hardware or security assumptions. Our approach, which is based on sorting networks and novel provably-oblivious constructions, is conceptually simple, easily verifiable, and very efficient in practice. Its data-independent algorithmic structure makes it secure in various different settings for remote computation, even in those that are known to be vulnerable to certain side-channel attacks (such as Intel SGX) or with strict requirements for low circuit complexity (like secure multiparty computation). We confirm that our approach is easily realizable through a compact implementation which matches our expectations for performance and is shown, both formally and empirically, to possess the desired security characteristics.

  匹配依据：MPC: secure multiparty computation; TEE: intel sgx

  </details>

- **Efficient and Fair Multiparty Protocols using Blockchain and Trusted Hardware**
  2020-02-10 · MPC / TEE · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2020/133)
  Souradyuti Paul, Ananya Shrivastava

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  In ACM CCS&#x27;17, Choudhuri et al. designed two fair public-ledger-based multi-party protocols (in the malicious model with dishonest majority) for computing an arbitrary function $f$. One of their protocols is based on a trusted hardware enclave $G$ (which can be implemented using Intel SGX-hardware) and a public ledger (which can be implemented using a blockchain platform, such as Ethereum). Subsequently, in NDSS&#x27;19, a stateless version of the protocol was published. This is the first time, (a certain definition of) fairness -- that guarantees either all parties learn the final output or nobody does -- is achieved without any monetary or computational penalties. However, these protocols are fair, if the underlying core MPC component guarantees both privacy and correctness. While privacy is easy to achieve (using a secret sharing scheme), correctness requires expensive operations (such as ZK proofs and commitment schemes). We improve on this work in three different directions: attack, design and performance. Our first major contribution is building practical attacks that demonstrate: if correctness is not satisfied then the fairness property of the aforementioned protocols collapse. Next, we design two new protocols -- stateful and stateless -- based on public ledger and trusted hardware that are: resistant against the aforementioned attacks, and made several orders of magnitude more efficient (related to both time and memory) than the existing ones by eliminating ZK proofs and commitment schemes in the design. Last but not the least, we implemented the core MPC part of our protocols using the SPDZ-2 framework to demonstrate the feasibility of its practical implementation.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing; TEE: hardware enclave, intel sgx

  </details>

- **Rerandomizable Garbling Beyond BHHO-KMHE and a Construction from LWE**
  2026-10-28 · MPC · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2664)
  Raphael Heitjohann, Jonas von der Heyden, Tibor Jager

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Rerandomizable garbling schemes (RGS) are a fundamental primitive enabling advanced cryptographic constructions such as multi-hop homomorphic encryption (Gentry, Halevi, Vaikuntanathan, CRYPTO 2010), iO-combiners (Ananth, Jain, Naor, Sahai, Yogev, CRYPTO 2016), and YOSO-style MPC (Acharya, Hazay, Kolesnikov, Prabhakaran, TCC 2022 and CRYPTO 2024). All known RGS instantiations rely on discrete-logarithm-type assumptions, concretely via the BHHO scheme (Boneh, Halevi, Hamburg, Ostrovsky, CRYPTO 2008) and its recent pairing-based variant (Heitjohann, von der Heyden, Jager, CRYPTO 2025). This reliance stems from the use of key-and-message homomorphic encryption (KMHE) that supports rerandomization and strong &quot;key-privacy under leakage&quot;, which hides the applied homomorphic transformations and is currently only achievable using BHHO-style bitwise encryption in combination with permutation-based homomorphisms. Our first main contribution is a new garbling technique that shifts the burden of hiding homomorphic transformations from the encryption scheme to the garbling itself. This allows us to construct RGS from KMHE schemes with substantially weaker properties, avoiding the need for bitwise encryption and permutation-based homomorphisms, and enabling the construction of RGS from KMHE with other homomorphisms, such as additively-homomorphic ones. As a second contribution, we give a concrete lattice-based instantiation of the required KMHE primitive, based on LWE. This construction is a variant of the GSW FHE scheme (Gentry, Sahai, Waters, CRYPTO 2013), which uses new techniques for rerandomization and is tailored to the requirements of our new garbling scheme by supporting a &quot;homomorphic&quot;/&quot;lossy&quot; mode. This yields the first RGS construction that does not rely on discrete-logarithm assumptions and may provide post-quantum security.

  匹配依据：MPC: garbling scheme, garbling schemes

  </details>

- **OblivDGL: Oblivious Deep Graph Learning Made Practical**
  2026-10-27 · MPC · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2655)
  Yiming Qin, Xiaoning Liu, Shangqi Lai, Joseph K. Liu, Xingliang Yuan

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  The rapid deployment of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) within Machine Learning as a Service (MLaaS) has opened up new privacy concerns. Both sensitive graph data and proprietary GNN models are submitted to and processed in third-party MLaaS platform for training and inference. To alleviate those concerns, recent efforts have been made to design tailored secure computation protocols for GNNs. Unfortunately, existing designs cannot accomplish security, functionality, and scalability simultaneously. They leak a certain degree of graph information, offer limited support on secure training of GNNs, and can hardly scale to large graphs. In this paper, we design and implement OblivDGL, an oblivious deep graph learning framework for secure GNN inference and training. Our design is inspired by Deep Graph Library (DGL), an industrial practice for graph learning. At its core, we distill the secure computational patterns of GNNs into a generalized form, and empower both secure GNN training and inference through a novel oblivious message passing paradigm. To realize such a paradigm, we design a new oblivious graph representation, and realize it by function secret sharing (FSS), a lightweight secure computation technique with low latency. Compared to prior secure GNN systems, OblivDGL achieves the most stringent privacy guarantees, i.e., revealing no private information except for the total number of edges and nodes. One standout feature of OblivDGL is the scalability of processing encrypted graphs by carefully tailored parallelization designs. Extensive evaluations on four benchmark graph datasets demonstrate that, compared to state-of-the-art secure GNN frameworks, OblivDGL reduces communication cost by up to 1024x and achieves up to 14.3x speedup in runtime during secure training. For secure inference, OblivDGL achieves up to 754x lower communication and a 4.19x speedup.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing, secure computation

  </details>

- **Asynchronous Verifiable and Complete Secret Sharing: From Design Patterns to System-Level Trade-offs**
  2026-10-27 · MPC · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37234)
  Joachim Bruneau-Queyreix, Martin Zivojinovic, Leo Mendiboure, Tom Claudel, Laurent Réveillère

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Modern secret sharing protocols promise robust secret sharing in fully asynchronous Byzantine systems, but their practical costs remain difficult to compare across papers, assumptions, and workloads. The difficulty is not merely experimental: protocols with similar asymptotic guarantees often place very different work on the critical path through their choices of dissemination, verification, batching, and recovery. This paper turns that fragmented research landscape into a corpus-backed designspace analysis and systems evaluation of asynchronous verifiable and complete secret sharing. We derive a design sieve, select seven representative protocols, and implement them in a common Rust framework. In our experiments on the Grid&#x27;5000 platform, we evaluate honest-dealer and faulty-dealer stress executions using latency, throughput, message count, bandwidth, and aggregate CPU-time. The results show that message complexity alone poorly predicts latency, that optimistic paths can be dominated by recovery cost, and that batching or packing helps only when verification stays off the critical path. These findings turn protocol-by-protocol comparisons into design-to-cost guidance for choosing, implementing, and extending asynchronous verifiable and complete sharing protocols.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing

  </details>

- **Reverse Substitution in Secret Sharing: The Critical One-Half Threshold and a Route to Superpolynomial Lower Bounds**
  2026-10-26 · MPC · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2652)
  Shahram Khazaei

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  The contribution vector (convec) of a secret-sharing scheme is the vector of its normalized share sizes. The average and maximum coordinates of a convec give, respectively, the average and maximum information ratios of the scheme. Obtaining superlinear lower bounds on these quantities for unrestricted perfect secret sharing has remained a challenging open problem for about four decades. In this paper, we study substitution, a natural way to build complicated access structures from simpler ones: one participant of an outer access structure is replaced by an inner access structure. Given secret-sharing schemes for the two factors, the standard forward construction composes them into a scheme for the composite access structure. We study the converse question. Given an arbitrary scheme for the composite access structure, we ask to what extent its convec admits a reverse factorization into convecs for the outer and inner factors, up to a common multiplicative loss. Exact reversal is false: we give a counterexample whose optimal reverse factor is \(8/9\), with a composite scheme that is scalar-linear over every finite field. On the positive side, we prove that a factor \(1/2\) is always attainable, and that every fixed instance admits a strictly larger factor. For a recursive family built from Csirmaz’s classical access structure \(\mathcal C_k\), whose distinguished set has size \(k\), we identify a critical reverse factor that determines when the resulting lower bound becomes superlinear. This critical factor exceeds one half by only an amount of order \((\log k)/k\). Crossing it yields superlinear lower bounds, while any fixed positive excess above one half gives a route to superpolynomial lower bounds. Using only Shannon inequalities, the corresponding recursive factor cannot cross the critical value. Thus any improvement sufficient to pass this threshold must exploit constraints beyond the Shannon inequalities.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing

  </details>

- **Minimality of Binary Codes From Weight Layers and Graph Cut Spaces**
  2026-10-26 · MPC · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35372)
  Xianhong Xie, Mengni Wang, Tingting Wu

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Minimal binary linear codes play an important role in secret-sharing schemes and in the structural study of linear codes. We study the minimality of three classes of known constructions: codes from a single complete Hamming-weight layer, codes from arbitrary unions of such layers and graph cut-space codes. For the previously studied single-layer codes C, we give a complete minimality classification: C is minimal if and only if t is even. For t = 4, we determine the minimum and maximum weights, and show that the family strictly violates the binary Ashikhmin Barg sufficient condition for every k. We also calculate the minimum distance of the dual code. For arbitrary unions of complete Hamming-weight layers, we obtain an if-and-only-if classification of minimality and uniform criteria for evenness, self-orthogonality, the doubly even property and hull dimension. We further analyze the family for odd k. Finally, using the classical bond characterization of cuts, we translate minimality of graph cut space codes into a graph-theoretic condition: a nonempty simple graph has a minimal cut code precisely when it has one edge-containing component and that component is complete. We also give a graph-function realization of the known binary tetrahedron code and explicitly identify the resulting code equivalence.

  匹配依据：MPC: secret sharing

  </details>

- **Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization**
  2026-10-26 · MPC · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.35833)
  Shreya Meel, Sennur Ulukus, Itzhak Tamo

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  In federated learning (FL), secure aggregation enables a server to compute the sum of local model updates of $N$ clients, without revealing any information on the individual model updates to the server, beyond their sum. Different clients may be subject to heterogeneous bandwidth constraints, and consequently may choose different numbers of quantization levels to represent the information they send. Most secure aggregation works require the clients to project the values of their update parameters to a common finite group (or field), which does not directly accommodate heterogeneous precision constraints on their transmitted masked updates. Existing approaches of secure aggregation with heterogeneous quantization levels reveal partial aggregates of model-updates, and can reveal segments of individual model updates, under certain dropout and client-server collusion patterns. To prevent this privacy breach, we propose an information-theoretic secure aggregation scheme that tolerates client drop-outs, and up to $T$ semi-honest clients that collude with each other and with the server, under heterogeneous quantization at clients. Our protocol utilizes the $(T+1, N)$ threshold black-box secret sharing construction, where secret shares of the client updates, despite belonging to distinct algebraic groups owing to different quantization, are generated from identical linear integer systems.

- **HELLO, GOODBYE: Concurrent General Composition From Super-Rushing Security**
  2026-10-26 · MPC · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2651)
  Anirudh Chandramouli

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Kushilevitz, Lindell, and Rabin (STOC `06, SIAM Journal on Computing `10), in their seminal result, showed that any standalone-secure synchronous multiparty computation (MPC) protocol can be compiled into one secure under concurrent general composition, by adding a synchronisation step after every round; thereby, at least doubling the round complexity. We show that for protocols that are secure against super-rushing adversaries, introduced by Asharov, Chandramouli, Cohen, and Ishai (EuroCrypt `25), two synchronisation rounds suffice. Specifically, for an $R$-round protocol that is secure against super-rushing adversaries with a black-box, straight-line simulator, adding a round of start synchronisation (saying ``HELLO&#x27;&#x27;) and a round of end synchronisation (saying ``GOODBYE&#x27;&#x27;) yields security under concurrent general composition with selective abort in $R+2$ rounds. If the end synchronisation is over a broadcast channel, the security is upgraded to unanimous abort. Both compilers incur no loss in the security reduction and preserve the flavour of security (perfect, statistical, or computational) of the underlying synchronous protocol. Moreover, combining with the sufficient conditions of Asharov et al. for perfect security, and the round-preserving super-rushing compilers of Ciampi, Ravi, and Zou (Cryptology ePrint Archive 2026/1745) for statistical and computational security, yields compilers from rushing security to security under concurrent general composition, with an additive overhead of at most $2$ rounds. We further extend our compilers to protocols with a trusted setup, such as a common reference string or a public-key infrastructure, which is necessary in the dishonest majority setting. We require two conditions. First, every execution of the protocol uses its own stateless copy of the setup, whose responses to the adversary do not depend on the interactions of the honest parties. In particular, this rules out setups that are shared across executions, such as a global common reference string or a single public-key infrastructure used by every execution. Second, the underlying protocol is secure against super-rushing adversaries with adaptive inputs, that is, even when the inputs are chosen after interacting with the setup. Under these conditions, the same compilers yield security under concurrent general composition. We also show that adaptive inputs cannot be relaxed to the usual notion of security in the setup-hybrid model. Specifically, we give a protocol that is statistically secure against super-rushing adversaries with guaranteed output delivery under the standard hybrid model, but is insecure under concurrent general composition after adding start and end synchronisation, even with selective abort.

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  As a core component of modern RAG systems, approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search has been extensively studied for decades. In practice, deploying ANN often requires symmetric privacy, where the querier&#x27;s query and the database owner&#x27;s data must remain hidden from each other, necessitating a secure multi-party computation (MPC) solution. So far, most MPC-based ANN protocols follow a cluster-based approach: they evaluate distances for the query over a large candidate set and rely on heavyweight primitives such as distributed ORAM to hide access patterns. As a result, each search typically requires $O(\sqrt{N})$ time. We propose HNSecW, a novel MPC protocol for ANN search that achieves the $O(\log N)$ search time for the first time. We first study the single-query setting. Starting from HNSW, the state-of-the-art ANN algorithm, we redesign its control flow and data structures to achieve fully data-independent execution. To further achieve logarithmic search time, we employ offline reshuffling and partial database duplication. Furthermore, we extend our protocol to support multiple sequential queries by introducing a &quot;double visited&quot; caching structure that eliminates redundant cross-query memory accesses, thereby avoiding per-query online shuffling. In addition, we develop a batch-query protocol that exploits higher parallelism to reduce both round complexity and the circuit&#x27;s critical path. - **Tritone: Pairwise Garbled Disputes for Multi-Party Proof Verification on Bitcoin**
  2026-10-23 · MPC · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2612)
  Oleksii Avramenko, Alessandro Baccarini, Torben Poguntke

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

Conventional federated bridges instead authorize withdrawals through a signing quorum, whose collusion can release funds without valid evidence. We present the Tritone protocol, which lets Bitcoin enforce the outcome of verifying a Groth16 proof for an NP relation fixed in a one-time trusted setup, with the locked funds secure as long as one of a fixed set of $N$ operators is honest. Verification is optimistic and off-chain, and every transaction is standard under current relay policy, so Tritone runs on Bitcoin today without consensus changes. Tritone generalizes the two-party BABE protocol to a fixed committee of $N$ operators, with one dispute instance per ordered pair. Cut-and-choose protects against malicious garblers, while Feldman verifiable secret sharing correlates input keys across candidates. Our new Lamport-adaptor gadget forces a challenging verifier to disclose the shares selected by the prover&#x27;s committed proof element, providing the transaction-level binding left unspecified by BABE. A single set of disclosed shares then unlocks all retained candidates. We formalize the multi-party primitive, prove the protocol secure against up to $N-1$ statically corrupted operators, and specify its complete pre-signed transaction graph. We implement Tritone in Rust. On Bitcoin mainnet, when one verifier disputes a claim at every stage, the prover-candidate posts 9,607 vB and the verifier 18,160 vB of protocol transactions. In local benchmarks at 40-bit statistical security, the prover-candidate of each dispute instance retains as little as 112.83 MiB. Tritone thus replaces trust in a signing quorum with a single-honest-operator assumption wherever locked bitcoin is released to an operator against a Groth16 proof, with Bitcoin bridges as our showcase.

This missing capability is particularly relevant in realistic distributed settings, where compromised participants may either expose valid shares or maliciously interfere with reconstruction. Combining this method with the evolving scheme of Cheng et al.\ (ASIACRYPT 2025), we obtain an evolving $k$-threshold scheme whose $t$-th share has size \[ \left\lfloor \frac{k}{2} \right\rfloor \log_2 t + O_k\!\left(\ell+\log_2\log_2 t\right) \] bits for an $\ell$-bit secret. The framework characterizes authorized, forbidden, and intermediate coalitions using restricted parity-check matrices and binary linear algebra, and introduces the accessible logical dimension \(κ(A)\), defined through the symplectic rank of locally supported logical classes, to refine the characterization of intermediate coalitions. We also show that participant partitioning can substantially improve block-level security and reconstruction thresholds. While these gradient-guided optimized FL methods improve the model accuracy, their reliance on sharing additional gradient information introduces a previously unexplored privacy vulnerability. Through the server, the client can privately choose and run quantum computations, prepare quantum states, and process quantum states supplied by other parties. Together, these capabilities let a purely classical party act as a quantum party in a variety of interactive protocols. We expect this virtual quantum computer to be a broadly useful tool.   2026-10-22 · MPC · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31814)

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  At CRYPTO 2007, Damgård and Nielsen introduced a preprocessing approach to multi-party computation (MPC) to achieve linear communication complexity. Another approach to reduce communication complexity was proposed by Cramer, Damgård, and de Haan at EUROCRYPT 2007, which involved using ramp-secret sharing schemes to jointly share base-field components of secrets from the extension field. In this paper, we combine these two ideas to achieve a non-asymptotic reduction of communication cost in a multi-phase MPC setup. We introduce a new modification of the ramp secret sharing scheme, called compact sharing, and tailor the MPC protocol to accommodate this modification. Compact sharing masks the polynomial coefficients that would otherwise leak during degree reduction. The protocol provides perfect security against static semi-honest adversaries under an explicit tradeoff between the corruption threshold and the extension degree. When the extension degree scales linearly with the number of parties, the gate-evaluation core achieves constant communication overhead relative to an extension-field element, amortized over full preprocessing batches; input and output communication is counted separately.

- **A Spectral Theory of Local-to-Global Leakage**
  2026-10-20 · MPC · [IACR ePrint](https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/2571)
  Rei Ueno

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  This paper studies how local leakages characterize the global leakage in additive secret sharing over a finite abelian group, which is a special case of linear secret sharing and side-channel masking. Our main finding is structural: local-to-global leakage is governed by two disjoint components---the magnitude of local leakage and its spectral alignment across shares, while existing literature attempted to characterize the global leakage only by local mutual information (MI). We first give an exact decomposition of leakage in additive secret sharing. The decomposition reveals a structural parameter invisible to MI, while previous literature conjectured that the local MI alone suffices to characterize global leakage. We then show that this missing parameter is indispensable: two leakage channels with identical local MI can induce exponentially different global leakage. Our exact decomposition identifies the missing structural quantity and completely characterizes this phenomenon. We then show the separation theorem with its realizability---local MI, despite governing the classical leakage bounds, does not even determine the exponential rate at which leakage vanishes under homomorphic composition. More strongly, we establish a universal separation theorem: even when all permutation-invariant scalar measures of local leakage agree, the global leakage can exhibit exponentially different decay rates. We further provide the characterization of the spectral alignment factor and derive its lower bound through character-order multiplicity and Möbius inversion. We then extend the framework to automorphism-weighted sharing. We establish that automorphism-weighted sharing can achieve perfect leakage cancellation with finitely many shares, even for non-trivial full-support local leakage channels. In sharp contrast, such perfect cancellation is impossible for ordinary additive sharing with non-trivial i.i.d local leakage channels and finitely many shares. Consequently, local leakage magnitudes correctly measure the average amount of local leakage, but discard the compatibility structure needed for composition. Magnitude-only bounds must optimize over structural alignments that the actual leakage channel does not realize.

  Sharding blockchains enhance scalability by distributing the workload across multiple shards. We propose QuarkShard, a sharding protocol that breaks away from this traditional paradigm to achieve intra-shard and cross-shard overheads below the lower bounds imposed by conventional approaches. QuarkShard decomposes cross-shard requests into single-input-shard transactions, where each transaction requires consensus and processing within only a single shard, thereby substantially reducing total request processing overhead. Meanwhile, through a carefully designed request decomposition algorithm, QuarkShard guarantees fund atomicity or location atomicity during request execution. QuarkShard also enhances the security of blockchain sharding systems against MEV attacks and flooding attacks. Independently, the separable associated-data transform yields a four-encryption nonce-misuse distinguisher with advantage $1-2^{-n}$, a deterministic AD-only forgery, and nonempty-message forgeries obtained from cross-domain state differences. - **On the Complexity of Symmetric Boolean Functions in Multiparty Private Simultaneous Messages**
  2026-10-15 · MPC · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21216)
  Marshall Ball, Peter Crawford-Kahrl, Vladimir Podolskii, Morgan Prior

  <details><summary>摘要 / Abstract</summary>

  Multiparty Private Simultaneous Messages (PSM), also known as Decomposable Randomized Encoding (DRE) or information-theoretic garbling, is a model for non-interactive secure computation. Each party encodes its input using shared randomness and sends a message to an evaluator who does not know that randomness. The evaluator must recover the function output without learning anything else about the inputs. Perfect privacy requires identical transcript distributions on inputs with the same output. We also study the weaker notion of support privacy, which requires only that these distributions have the same support. We study the communication complexity of symmetric Boolean functions when each of the $n$ parties holds one input bit. Lower bounds. We prove a superlinear lower bound for support-private PSM protocols computing $OR_n$. Our technique gives $Ω(n\log n)$ lower bounds for $MAJ_n$ and $EMAJ_n$ (with even $n$), and an $Ω(n\log q)$ lower bound for $MOD_q$ when $q\leq(1-c)n$ for a fixed constant $c&gt;0$. Upper bounds. We construct perfectly private PSM protocols of total communication $\widetilde{O}(n^{3/2})$ for every symmetric Boolean function, improving on the known quadratic bound. For $MAJ_n$, known branching-program constructions yield an upper bound of $O(n\log^3 n\log\log n)$. For $EMAJ_n$ and $MOD_q$ with prime $q$, the lower bounds are tight up to constant factors in the stated regimes. Under support privacy, we obtain $\widetilde{O}(n)$ communication for every symmetric Boolean function. Earlier lower-bound techniques of Ball et al. (ITCS 2020) yield only trivial linear bounds for symmetric Boolean functions. Concurrent and independent work by Holmgren and Wu proves a $ω(n)$ lower bound for $OR_n$ using the same combinatorial core. Both works used AI assistance.

We ask how small the difference table can be on unit differences when the residue permutation is fixed and only higher coefficient digits of its lift are chosen. - **HULK: An Efficient Algorithm for Enabling Fast Bulk Bitwise Operations on Homomorphically Encrypted Data**
  2026-10-13 · MPC · [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18391)
  Mayank Kabra, Phillip Widdowson, Harshita Gupta, Rakesh Nadig, Nisa Bostancı, Eirini Tzermpou, Rakesh Kumar, Spiros Galanopoulos, Ataberk Olgun, Abdullah Giray Yağlıkçı, Mohammad Sadrosadati, Onur Mutlu

The method is automated and general-purpose, and composes with existing multiplicative-complexity optimization. Experiments show that it reduces jointly evaluated computation and improves end-to-end GC performance on circuits with party-local structure, revealing protocol-cost savings missed by conventional GC cost models.
